chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
On the Day of Resurrection, something like a globe will come, so it will push the believer in the back and enter him into Paradise, and it will be said: 'This is righteousness.'

key_terms.الْبِرُّ: Righteousness (specifically filial piety in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the physical sign of righteousness that appears on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this unique eschatological narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes a physical entity resembling a 'kubbah' (often interpreted as a globe or a specific bodily part like the nape) that pushes the believer into Paradise, serving as the tangible manifestation of 'al-Birr'. While the chapter title links this to righteousness with parents, Shia scholars often view this as a metaphor for the ultimate reward of filial piety, where the act itself becomes the vehicle for entry into Jannah. This highlights the transformative power of 'Birr' in Shia theology, elevating it from mere social duty to a cosmic mechanism of salvation.
